page.layout: One page of text: a centred title "EPIGRAMMATA." at the top; below it one column of verse in four stanzas, with the author's name "GEORG. REMUS." set at the right; then a woodcut ornament; and at the lower right the title "ALIVD" in capitals.

p.i: Rari quidem superstant. Tundi, premique & uri, Mediásque sæpè flammas Transfire nos necessum, & Cædi calumniarum Turpi pios flagello.
BENE ast habet. quiescens Obdurat, atque vincit TOLERANTIA omne durum.
Nam SPES adest ab æthrâ, Spes alma, natâ cœlo, Subnixa magno JESU, Qui Gratiâ benignos Irrorat unus imbreis.
Hæc SPES(viden'?) triumphat, Suos locans Olympo.

page.notes: The single "C" above the title is a printed mark at the top of the page. It is transcribed as a paragraph. A woodcut ornament sits below the verse: a cornucopia-like design with a central face or mask, flowers at the top, and hanging tassels and scrolls below. It has no text. The reading "Cædi" is a ligature and could also be "Cadi"; it is as printed. "(viden'?)" is printed in the text with the apostrophe and question mark, not added by transcription. "ALIVD" is a title of the following epigram, set apart in capitals; I have taken it as a level 2 heading.
